newsitem.title: USA: Marine to head U.S. forces in Latin America.
newsitem.headline: Marine to head U.S. forces in Latin America.

text.p: President Bill Clinton nominated Marine Corps Lt. Gen. Charles Wilhelm on Friday to be commander of U.S. military forces in Latin America, the Caribbean and the Gulf of Mexico.

Wilhelm, 55, must be confirmed by the Senate to be promoted to full general and become chief of the U.S. military's Southern Command, now in the process of moving its headquarters from Panama to Miami.
Wilhelm, currently head of U.S. Marine forces in the Atlantic region, would succeed Army Gen. Wesley Clark, who recently became supreme allied commander of all NATO allied forces in Europe (SACEUR).

In addition to North-South military ties, the Southern Command is considered a major link between Washington and Latin American capitals in the war against illegal narcotics flowing to the United States.
Wilhelm, a native of Edenton, North Carolina, and a 33-year military veteran, is a decorated Vietnam War veteran and has served in posts around the world, including the Philippines and Somalia.
The move is an historic step for the Marine Corps, which has never had two chiefs of major regional U.S. military commands at the same time.
Marine Gen. Anthony Zinni was recently named head of the Central Command in Tampa, Florida, with responsibility for all American forces in the key Gulf region near Iraq and Iran.

The Pentagon announced in May that responsibilities of the Southern Command had been expanded from oversight over U.S. military ties with Central and South American nations to include the Caribbean and its island nations and the Gulf of Mexico.
The move was made chiefly to improve integration of counter-drug efforts in the hemisphere by giving one commander responsibility for both the source and transit zones of the drug trade.
Wilhelm is a graduate of Florida Southern College and holds a masters from Salve Regina College. He is graduated from the U.S. Naval War College.
